Job Context (circumstances & environment surrounding the job)

Group Audit (GA) consists of a Bahrain-based team plus local Internal Audit teams based in overseas units of ABC. GA is responsible for providing independent assurance on the adequacy and effectiveness of ABC’s internal controls to the Executive Management and the Board of ABC (via the Audit Committee). This is achieved by completing Audit assignments according to a risk-based Annual Audit Plan. The findings of the Audit assignments are included within published Audit Reports which contain findings requiring management to undertake corrective actions to address any control weaknesses identified. Findings are also presented to the Audit Committee of the Board of ABC on a quarterly basis. Given the nature of GA’s role within the business, the job holder is expected to uphold the highest standards of integrity and confidentiality at all times. The volume, importance and confidentiality of the material with which the job holder will deal with will require a strong sense of discretion and the ability to organise and present material in a cogent way. Group Audit staffs liaise with individuals at all levels within the organisation, including Executive Management and Board members. The job holder will be required to conduct all interactions with courtesy, respect and professionalism.

The CMM Programmer develops, validates, optimizes, and maintains Coordinate Measuring Machine (CMM) programs and dimensional inspection methods for vehicle launch and series production at Lucid Motors. Reporting to the Metrology Manager, this role ensures efficient, accurate, repeatable, and traceable measurement of stamped parts, body structures, closures, assemblies, fixtures, tooling, Powertrain components, and investigation samples. The CMM Programmer works closely with Dimensional Engineering, Manufacturing, Product Engineering, Supplier Quality, Tooling, and Metrology Technicians to translate engineering requirements into reliable measurement strategies and actionable dimensional reports.
q: Advanced CMM programming and measurement capabilities, including CAD-based programming, offline programming, alignments, datum setup, probe qualification, scanning, feature construction, reporting, and troubleshooting.
Strong knowledge of GD&T, datum reference frames, tolerance interpretation, coordinate metrology, measurement uncertainty, MSA, repeatability, and correlation methods.
Experience with common CMM software platforms and dimensional data analysis or reporting tools.
Ability to interpret complex engineering drawings, CAD models, specifications, measurement plans, and automotive dimensional control requirements.
Working knowledge of optical measurement, ScanBox, eCube or inline measurement systems, laser scanning, checking fixtures, master parts, and manual metrology.
Understanding of stamping, BIW, closures, tooling, vehicle assembly, precision components, and manufacturing variation.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, technical documentation, organizational, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and familiarity with PLM, QMS, MES, metrology databases, and digital traceability systems.
Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Automotive Engineering, Metrology, or a related discipline.
2-5 years of hands-on CMM programming and dimensional measurement experience within automotive, aerospace, precision manufacturing, or a comparable industry.
Demonstrated ability to independently create, validate, optimize, and release CMM programs and interpret measurement results against GD&T requirements.
Ability to work in a metrology laboratory and on the manufacturing floor, support production priorities, and communicate complex technical findings across organizational levels.
Experience with offline CMM programming, CAD-based inspection, probe-system configuration, scanning strategies, MSA, correlation, and capability analysis.
Experience measuring stamped parts, body structures, closures, fixtures, tooling, precision assemblies, or automotive components.
Experience supporting new product launches, greenfield manufacturing, safe launch, or high-volume production ramp-up.

r: Develop, prove out, validate, optimize, document, and maintain CMM programs using approved CAD models, engineering drawings, GD&T, measurement plans, and acceptance criteria.
Define robust part alignments, datum structures, probing strategies, feature constructions, scanning paths, clearance moves, measurement sequences, and reporting outputs.
Create and maintain inspection programs for stamped panels, Body-in-White (BIW), closures, assemblies, fixtures, tooling, master parts, Powertrain components, and investigation samples.
Validate new and revised programs through feature verification, repeatability studies, correlation, peer review, and comparison with approved reference methods.

Generate clear dimensional reports, deviation summaries, trend and SPC charts, color maps, and technical findings for launch, production, audits, containment, and root cause investigations.
Support fixture buyoff, tooling verification, engineering changes, new-part introduction, trial builds, safe launch, process validation, and dimensional sign-off.
Troubleshoot CMM programs, probe configurations, alignments, software errors, collisions, environmental effects, and inconsistent measurement results.
Maintain program revision control, backups, naming conventions, report templates, probe libraries, qualification records, calibration status, and measurement traceability.
Coordinate with Metrology Technicians to ensure correct program execution, part setup, fixture use, data storage, and escalation of abnormal results.
Provide training and technical coaching on CMM operation, program execution, GD&T interpretation, measurement methods, reporting, and equipment care.
Support continuous improvement of programming standards, measurement cycle time, automation, data visualization, correlation, and metrology workflows.

d: Lucidya is an AI-native platform for customer experience (CX) intelligence that helps organizations understand their customers and take action across the entire customer lifecycle.

Our platform brings together products including Social Listening, OmniServe, Survey, and AI Agent, helping enterprise organizations across the region turn customer data into better experiences and measurable business outcomes.

As Lucidya continues to scale, our products are becoming more sophisticated and our customers more demanding. Design has an increasingly important role to play in making sure that complexity doesn't become the customer's problem.
At this level, we're looking for someone who can move beyond simply executing designs and own problems from beginning to end.

You'll take ambiguous customer and business problems, work with Product and Engineering to understand what we're trying to achieve, explore different approaches, and drive the design through to implementation and iteration.

You'll be working on products that can involve significant amounts of data, complex workflows, AI-powered functionality, and bilingual experiences. The challenge isn't simply making these products look good — it's making them easy to understand, efficient to use, and genuinely useful for enterprise customers.

You'll have meaningful independence, but you're not expected to operate alone. You'll work alongside senior designers, Product Managers, Engineers, UX researchers, and UX writers. The strongest person in this role will know when to push their own thinking, when to ask for input, and when to challenge an assumption.
q: You can own a problem without needing someone to tell you every step. You know how to take an ambiguous brief, ask the right questions, break it down, and move it forward.

You think like a product designer, not just a UI designer. You're interested in the customer, the business problem, the constraints, and the outcome — not simply whether the final interface looks polished.

You're comfortable challenging the status quo. If you think a requirement doesn't make sense or there's a better way to solve a problem, you're willing to say so and can back your thinking with evidence.
You know when to push and when to compromise. You can defend an important design decision while understanding that product development involves technical, commercial, and time constraints.
You're highly collaborative. You don't throw designs over the wall to Engineering or wait for Product to tell you what to do. You work with people throughout the process.

You're comfortable with ambiguity and change. Priorities may shift, requirements may evolve, and not every decision will be made for you. You stay focused on the outcome rather than becoming frustrated by the process.

You're genuinely curious about users. You want to understand why customers behave the way they do and are willing to change your design when the evidence tells you that your original assumption was wrong.

You communicate with clarity. You can explain complex design decisions to people who aren't designers and can adapt how you communicate depending on whether you're speaking with an Engineer, Product Manager, customer, or executive.

You care about quality. You have high standards for interaction, usability, accessibility, and visual design, but you also understand when “good enough to learn” is better than spending weeks perfecting something nobody has validated.
You have 3–5 years of product design or UX/UI experience , ideally in B2B or SaaS environments, with a portfolio demonstrating genuine end-to-end product thinking.
You're proficient in Figma and comfortable with prototyping, design systems, and modern product design practices.
You're a Saudi national , as this position is designated for Saudi nationals.
Experience designing data-heavy or analytics-driven B2B products.
Experience with AI-powered products, conversational interfaces, or AI agents.
Experience designing Arabic/English or RTL experiences.
Familiarity with tools such as FigJam, Maze, LogRocket, or similar research and testing tools.
What the hiring process will look like
Recruiter screening — An initial conversation about your experience, motivations, and what you're looking for next.
Design interview — A deeper discussion with the Design team around your product thinking, design process, and approach to solving complex problems.
Portfolio / case study presentation — You'll take us through selected projects, focusing on the problem, your role, decisions, trade-offs, collaboration, and measurable or observable outcomes.
Team / culture interview — A conversation focused on how you work, give and receive feedback, handle disagreement, and contribute to a high-performing team.
Final interview — Final conversation with the relevant leadership team.
r: Own design problems end-to-end. You'll take ownership from understanding the problem and defining the user experience through wireframes, prototypes, high-fidelity UI, handoff, implementation, and post-launch iteration.

Turn ambiguity into clarity. Requirements won't always arrive perfectly defined. You'll work with Product, Engineering, Research, and stakeholders to understand the underlying problem and determine what we actually need to solve.

Design for outcomes, not outputs. You'll challenge solutions that don't clearly improve the customer's experience and use research, data, and customer feedback to understand whether your designs are actually working.

Partner closely with Product and Engineering. You'll be involved early rather than receiving requirements at the end of the process. You'll help shape what gets built and work through technical and product constraints without losing sight of the customer.
Raise the quality of our products. You'll contribute to Lucidya's design system and help create consistency across our products while knowing when a problem requires something different.

Bring customer evidence into design decisions. You'll conduct or support usability testing and lightweight research, using what you learn to validate assumptions rather than relying solely on personal opinion.

Make complex products feel simple. Whether you're designing analytics, workflows, AI functionality, or customer-facing experiences, you'll look for ways to reduce cognitive load and help users get to the outcome they need faster.
Design thoughtfully for our market. You'll account for Arabic and English experiences, RTL considerations, and the needs of enterprise customers across the region.
Communicate your thinking clearly. You'll present work to Product, Engineering, leadership, and other stakeholders, explaining not only what you designed but why you made those decisions.

Make the team better. You'll actively participate in critiques, give thoughtful feedback to other designers, and share what you've learned rather than keeping your knowledge within your own product area.

d: Reports To: Warehouse Supervisor / Supply Chain Manager

The Storekeeper is responsible for the accurate receiving, storage, issuing, and recording of raw materials, packaging materials, spare parts, consumables, and finished goods. The role ensures stock accuracy, product traceability, proper storage conditions, and timely material availability while complying with Amalfi Foods’ food-safety and quality standards.
q: Diploma or bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Logistics, Business Administration, Accounting, or a related field.
Minimum of two to three years of storekeeping or warehouse experience, preferably within food manufacturing or FMCG.
Good understanding of inventory control, FIFO, FEFO, batch tracking, and expiry management.
Experience using ERP, inventory-management, or warehouse-management systems.
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and basic inventory reporting.
Knowledge of food-safety, hygiene, and warehouse-storage requirements is preferred.
A valid forklift licence would be an advantage.
High level of accuracy and attention to detail.
Ability to work under pressure and meet production deadlines.
Ability to supervise warehouse helpers when required.
Physically capable of performing warehouse duties safely.
Willingness to work shifts, overtime, or weekends when operationally required.
Accuracy and timeliness of receiving and issuing transactions.
Compliance with FIFO and FEFO requirements.
Number of expired or damaged items caused by storage failures.
Availability of materials required for production.
Accuracy of batch and expiry-date traceability.
Warehouse cleanliness, organization, and audit compliance.
Timely reporting of low-stock, slow-moving, and near-expiry inventory.
r: Receive raw materials, packaging materials, spare parts, and other supplies against approved purchase orders.
Verify quantities, batch numbers, production and expiry dates, and the condition of all deliveries.
Coordinate with Quality Control before accepting food ingredients and packaging materials.
Report shortages, damaged items, quality concerns, or delivery discrepancies immediately.
Prepare and maintain Goods Received Notes and supporting documentation.
Store all materials in their designated locations according to food-safety requirements.
Maintain clear identification of every item, including item code, batch number, quantity, receipt date, and expiry date.
Apply FIFO and FEFO principles consistently.
Monitor minimum, maximum, reorder, and safety-stock levels.
Maintain accurate records of all stock movements in the ERP system or approved stock-control records.
Conduct daily checks, cycle counts, and monthly physical stock counts.
Investigate and report stock variances, damages, expired materials, and slow-moving inventory.
Ensure allergens, chemicals, food ingredients, packaging materials, spare parts, and finished goods are properly segregated.
Issue materials only against approved production requisitions or authorized requests.
Ensure the correct item, batch, and quantity are issued to production.
Record all issues, transfers, and returns accurately and without delay.
Receive unused materials returned from production, inspect their condition, and return acceptable stock to the appropriate location.
Maintain complete traceability from receipt through issuance and return.
Receive finished products from production and verify quantities and batch details.
Arrange finished goods systematically by product, batch, production date, and expiry date.
Prepare and issue products according to approved sales orders and dispatch instructions.
Verify loaded quantities and support the preparation of dispatch documentation.
Coordinate closely with production, sales, and distribution teams to ensure timely dispatch.
Maintain the warehouse in a clean, organized, safe, and audit-ready condition.
Monitor and document required storage temperatures and environmental conditions.
Follow FSSC 22000, HACCP, Halal, GMP, hygiene, and company quality procedures.
Support pest-control inspections and ensure materials are protected from contamination.
Identify and isolate rejected, damaged, expired, or non-conforming stock in designated quarantine areas.
Follow workplace health and safety requirements, including safe stacking and material handling.
Participate in internal, external, customer, and certification audits.
Prepare daily and monthly reports covering receipts, issues, stock balances, variances, damages, expiries, and slow-moving items.
Notify management in advance of low-stock situations or materials approaching expiry.
Maintain properly filed and easily retrievable warehouse records.
Recommend improvements to storage arrangements, material flow, and inventory controls.
The Storekeeper is accountable for all materials under their custody. No stock may be received, issued, transferred, adjusted, or disposed of without the required documentation and authorization.
